transcript.content: Hello, welcome. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me. Um... well, I guess I came in because I've started doing some things at work—I do bookkeeping—and at school that... well, they don't really make a lot of sense. 

I hope it's okay to bring this up, I know it probably sounds a little silly. But I've been catching myself doing things like... lining receipts all across the floor, or, um, tapping the calculator in sets of nine. Just little routines, I guess? Or sometimes I'll just stand by the copier with my hands held up in the air until someone comes by and asks if I'm okay. 

It's really nothing too terrible, I don't want to make it sound worse than it is, but it is a little embarrassing. Is that... is that the right kind of thing I should be telling you?
When you find yourself doing these things, like tapping in sets of nine or holding your hands in the air, what is going through your mind?

Um, well... to be honest, I'm not really sure. It's not like I'm thinking about anything bad or anything. It's more like... my mind just kind of goes blank? Or maybe it's just that it feels like the right thing to do in the moment. 

I don't want to make it sound like I'm totally out of control or anything, because I'm not. I can still get my work done, you know? It's just... I guess I just kind of zone out for a second. Is that normal? Like, do other people ever do things like that when they're just really focused or maybe a little stressed? I hope I'm explaining this right.
Have you ever noticed yourself making repetitive sounds or noises, like throat clearing, sniffing, or words, that feel difficult to stop?

Um, no, I don't think I do anything like that. I mean, I might clear my throat if I'm actually sick or something, but not... not in a way that I can't stop. 

I try really hard to be quiet at work so I don't bother anyone else in the office. I hope that's a good thing? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right answers. Is it okay that I don't have that happening?
Have you ever heard voices or seen things that other people couldn't see or hear?

Um... well, I guess... sometimes? I mean, it's really nothing major, I promise. Just... occasionally, when I'm all alone at my desk, or maybe walking home from my classes, I'll hear this voice. 

It sounds like a man, and he just says really normal things, like... "check line seven" or "you missed the sign." It's so clear that I actually look around to see who's talking to me, but... there's never anyone there. 

It's probably just my brain being tired from all the numbers, right? Like, an overactive imagination because I'm trying so hard to do a good job? I really hope that doesn't sound too crazy. I mean, I know it's not real, so that means I'm okay, right? Is it alright that I'm telling you this?
Have you experienced any significant changes in your mood, like feeling intensely down and depressed, or unusually energetic and elated?

Um, well, I guess... sometimes my mood does change a bit, but I think it's mostly just normal stress from work and school, you know? 

Like, there are some weeks where I feel really, really good. Unusually sharp, I guess? Almost unstoppable. I'll get this burst of energy and feel like I can map out my entire future in just one night. It feels really productive, actually, so I hope that's a positive thing? 

But then... well, sometimes when I'm feeling like that, if my boss at the firm or maybe a classmate points out a tiny mistake I made... I might snap at them. Harder than I mean to, honestly. I always feel really bad about it right after. It's just that I get a little irritable when I'm so focused. 

That's not too unusual, is it? I mean, everyone gets a little cranky when they're working hard, right? I just want to make sure I'm giving you what you need. Is it okay that I get like that sometimes?
Have you heard that voice at times when your mood and energy felt completely normal?

Um... yeah, I guess so. I hope that doesn't make things too confusing? But, um, there was actually a stretch of several weeks a little while ago where my mood was totally regular. Like, I was sleeping a normal amount, and I didn't have that huge burst of energy I mentioned before. I was just... normal. 

But, um, I did still hear the voice sometimes during that stretch. And I still felt really... pulled into finding patterns in the numbers at work. I tried to just ignore it and focus on my job, though, so it wouldn't cause any problems. 

I really hope I'm giving you the right information. I just want to be as helpful as I can. Is it okay that I noticed that happening even when I felt completely fine?

Looking back over the entire time you have been having these experiences, would you say these periods of high energy and irritability have been happening most of the time, or only for a smaller part of the time?

Um, well, if I really look back at it all... I hope it doesn't make me sound like I'm out of control or anything, but... I guess those wired stretches, where I'm feeling really confident or getting a bit irritable? They've actually taken up more of the time overall than the calmer stretches. 

I mean, the intensity goes up and down, you know? It's not always super extreme. Sometimes it's just a little extra drive so I can get through all the ledgers at work. But yeah, if I'm being completely honest, the high energy has definitely been around for the majority of this whole period. 

I really hope that's helpful for you to know? I just want to make sure I'm answering right and giving you the full picture, even if it makes me sound a little... intense. Is it okay that it's been happening most of the time like that?
